title: Turn job planning on in athena.toml and record the decision
summary: Retry of job 5b: add [job_plan] (enabled, 0.75 caps, 600 s timeouts, max_rounds 3) to athena.toml and log the decision in docs/decisions.md. The earlier attempt showed that three existing tests (two in crates/, one test helper) assume the repo config has no [job_plan]. This reading allows test-only edits to those and no other changes under crates/. The audience is the owner and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check that tests parse and pass with planning on, not that the section merely exists.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check are required to pass.
One focused config change; code edits limited to test code.
The repo-config test enforces that athena.toml parses with the schema.
The decision entry cites the design's sections 7 and 9 and the baseline numbers.
Tests are made robust to the section wherever it sits, rather than patched for one instance.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The earlier verifier found that turning planning on breaks the assumptions of tests in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs, which read athena.toml. Those cannot pass without test-only edits. I take the goal (planning on, tests green) as the stated goal, so I allow those test-only edits and name them as deliverables.
The proposed retry text says not to edit those files and to stop and report. If the user wants that stricter rule, the job should stop and report instead; the question below asks which.
Production code of the planning stage and config schema stays unchanged; only test code and test helpers under crates/ may change.
The producer lists changed files at the end and confirms each is on the allowed list.
docs/design/job-planning.md gets only a small 'Built as' note, which must mention the extra test edits.
question: Is it acceptable to edit test code in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs? Without those edits the tests fail once planning is on. If you say no, the job should stop and report instead.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml has a [job_plan] section with enabled = true, planner_usd = 0.75, critic_usd = 0.75, planner_timeout_s = 600, critic_timeout_s = 600 and max_rounds = 3, with no unknown fields.
Run `cargo test --locked`: every test passes. This covers the repo-config test that parses athena.toml with planning enabled, crates/athena-cli/tests, run_pin_tests, and xtask's boundary test.

The only paths under crates/ that differ are test-only: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs, plus test code in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs. No non-test code in the planning stage or the config schema changed. The final output lists the changed files and confirms each is allowed.

Tests that need the unplanned path drop or ignore the [job_plan] section wherever it sits in athena.toml. Tests that append their own [job_plan] (job_plan.rs, config.rs unknown-key and defaults tests) do not end up with the section twice.

docs/decisions.md has a new numbered entry that turns planning on and cites docs/design/job-planning.md. It lists the alternatives from section 7. It gives the keep rule from section 9: metric is landed share of dispatched change jobs, baseline 64%, hold through 30 planned jobs unless it falls, decide at 100 jobs on 72% and a $2.50 cost ceiling per landed job. It gives the reversal: set enabled = false.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for turning job planning on that names athena.toml. The design doc's 'Built as' note mentions the test edits.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`; both pass.

out_of_scope: Changing the planning stage's production code or the [job_plan] schema
Merging the duplicated section-stripping helpers across crates
Measuring the keep rule's outcome; that happens after 30 and 100 planned jobs
departures: The retry widens scope to include the test-only edits that the earlier verifier found necessary. I raised the pass chance a little because that cause is now known.
